explanation.summary: The model estimates a 85% chance that this customer will churn, compared with 20% for a typical customer in the reference sample. The biggest factors raising the risk are Tenure: 1 month, Internet service: Fiber optic and Contract: Month-to-month. Factors lowering the risk are Total charges to date: $95.10 and Monthly charges: $95.10.
explanation.note: SHAP shows how much each input pushed this model's score up or down for this customer. It describes the model's behaviour learned from historical data, not proven causes of churn.

recommendations.title: Contact this customer proactively
recommendations.action: Have a retention specialist reach out soon to understand concerns before the customer decides to leave.
recommendations.why: The predicted probability is at or above the 60% high-risk cut-off.
evidence: Model: estimated churn probability is 85% (High risk).
recommendations.assumption: Assumes outreach is welcome; respect the customer's contact preferences.

recommendations.title: Strengthen early-life onboarding
recommendations.action: Schedule a welcome check-in, confirm the service is set up correctly and make sure the first bills are understood.
recommendations.why: The customer joined recently (1 month), and short tenure strongly raises predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Tenure = 1 month raises this customer's churn probability by about 26.6 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: customers in their first 0–6 months churned at 52.9%, versus 6.6% for customers with 61–72 months.
recommendations.assumption: Assumes early contact improves the experience; the data shows the pattern, not the effect of onboarding.

recommendations.title: Investigate the fiber service experience
recommendations.action: Review this customer's service quality and price against current fiber plans, and ask about any issues.
recommendations.why: Fiber optic internet raises this customer's predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Internet service = Fiber optic raises this customer's churn probability by about 7.1 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: fiber optic customers churned at 41.9%, versus 19.0% for DSL customers.
recommendations.assumption: The dataset does not record why fiber customers leave (price, reliability or competition); confirm with the customer before acting.

recommendations.title: Offer a longer contract with a clear benefit
recommendations.action: Propose a one- or two-year plan with a tangible incentive such as a price lock or loyalty discount.
recommendations.why: The month-to-month contract is one of the strongest reasons the model rates this customer as at risk.
evidence: Model: Contract = Month-to-month raises this customer's churn probability by about 5.5 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: month-to-month customers churned at 42.7%, versus 11.3% on one-year and 2.8% on two-year contracts.
recommendations.assumption: Assumes the customer is open to a longer commitment; the dataset does not show how customers react to offers.

recommendations.title: Encourage automatic payment
recommendations.action: Invite the customer to switch to automatic bank transfer or credit card payment, for example with a small one-time credit.
recommendations.why: Paying by electronic check raises this customer's predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Payment method = Electronic check raises this customer's churn probability by about 3.2 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: electronic-check payers churned at 45.3%, versus 15.2% for automatic credit-card payers.
recommendations.assumption: Payment method may reflect other habits; switching it alone may not change the customer's decision.

recommendations.title: Offer the online security add-on
recommendations.action: Offer a discounted or trial online security package and explain what it protects.
recommendations.why: Not having online security raises this customer's predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Online security = No raises this customer's churn probability by about 2.3 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: internet customers without online security churned at 41.8%, versus 14.6% for those with it.
recommendations.assumption: Customers who choose online security may differ in other ways, so adding it may not by itself reduce churn.

recommendations.title: Improve support follow-up
recommendations.action: Offer a free trial of tech support or a proactive support call to resolve open issues.
recommendations.why: Not having tech support raises this customer's predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Tech support = No raises this customer's churn probability by about 2.0 percentage points (SHAP).
Dataset: internet customers without tech support churned at 41.6%, versus 15.2% for those with it.
recommendations.assumption: Customers who choose tech support may differ in other ways, so adding it may not by itself reduce churn.

recommendations.title: Suggest a protection bundle
recommendations.action: Offer online backup and device protection as a bundled, low-cost add-on to increase the value of the service.
recommendations.why: Not having online backup and device protection raises this customer's predicted risk.
evidence: Model: Online backup = No raises this customer's churn probability by about 1.2 percentage points (SHAP).
Model: Device protection = No raises this customer's churn probability by about 0.5 percentage points (SHAP).
recommendations.assumption: Assumes extra services increase perceived value; uptake and its effect on churn are not measured in the data.
